title: Pure dimension
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. $X$ has *pure dimension $d$* (is *equidimensional of dimension $d$*) if every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] $Z$ of the underlying topological space $|X|$ has Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] $\dim Z=d$, where $Z$ carries the subspace topology (so $\dim Z$ is the supremum of the lengths $r$ of chains $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_r$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $Z$). The empty scheme has pure dimension $d$ for every $d$, having no irreducible components.
